title: r3 wrong-person TOCTOU backstop `mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person` is never called — apply_wrong_person still transitions via unguarded `update_reference_call_status`
evidence:
--- mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(reference_call_id: UUID)
UPDATE reference_call
SET status          = 'awaiting_correction'::reference_call_status,
    terminal_reason = 'contact_invalid',
    next_attempt_at = NULL,
    updated_at      = now()
WHERE id = $1
  AND status = 'contact_initiated'::reference_call_status
  AND taken_over_at IS NULL
RETURNING id::text;  AND  case
                sql.update_reference_call_status(
                  config.db,
                  id_uuid,
                  sql.AwaitingCorrection,
                  "",
                  "contact_invalid",
                  sql.ContactInitiated,
                )  AND  case row.taken_over_at != "" {
        True -> wisp.redirect(to: "/reference/" <> token)
detail: The new guarded SQL (taken_over_at IS NULL) has zero call sites; the handler still uses update_reference_call_status, whose only guard is status = contact_initiated — and take-over preserves that status. A take-over landing between the token read and the UPDATE still yanks the landlord-handled row into awaiting_correction: the exact race the r3 head commit claims to fix.
recommended_fix: Call sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(...) in apply_wrong_person's non-exhaust branch (handle 0 rows as stand-down), or add AND taken_over_at IS NULL AND correction_cycles = 0 to update_reference_call_status.sql.

title: Contact-fallback CASE in find_reference_call_by_send_ref: `WHEN rc.correction_cycles >= 1` arm is unreachable under the outer `rc.correction_cycles = 0` gate
evidence:
OR (rc.correction_cycles = 0 AND $1 <> '' AND CASE
         WHEN rc.correction_cycles >= 1 THEN NULLIF(rc.corrected_email, '')
         ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF(rc.corrected_email, ''), rc.contact_email)
       END = $1)
    OR (rc.correction_cycles = 0 AND $2 <> '' AND CASE
         WHEN rc.correction_cycles >= 1 THEN NULLIF(rc.corrected_phone, '')
         ELSE COALESCE(NULLIF(rc.corrected_phone, ''), rc.contact_phone)
       END = $2)
detail: Inside `rc.correction_cycles = 0` the >= 1 branch can never fire; both twins always take ELSE. Harmless today (the outer gate enforces the pre-correction-only intent) but it is dead complexity that misstates the rule and invites a wrong future edit.
recommended_fix: Drop the inner CASE entirely: under the outer = 0 gate the compare is simply COALESCE(NULLIF(rc.corrected_email, ''), rc.contact_email) = $1 (same for phone).

title: run_action_with_prechecks: a DB Error from verify_vacancy_active falls into the catch-all `_ -> action()` — the action proceeds on a failed precheck
detail: The `_` arm swallows Error(...) and 'no vacancy row' identically to 'vacancy not archived', so a DB failure during the archived-vacancy precheck still executes the mutation and returns 200. The outer verify_application_in_vacancy Error maps to 404 (misleading but safe); this one is not safe.
recommended_fix: Match Error(err) explicitly and return db_failure/500; keep `_` for the not-archived success path only.

title: send_is_post_correction timestamp regex is prefix-only — a malformed entry with a valid prefix still raises on the timestamptz cast
evidence:
CASE WHEN e->>'at' ~ '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}[T ][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}'
                THEN (e->>'at')::timestamptz >= rc.corrected_at
                ELSE false END
detail: The regex has no trailing anchor, so e.g. '2026-08-08T12:00:00garbage' passes the test and `(e->>'at')::timestamptz` throws, contradicting the r3 N9 comment that a malformed entry stands the event down instead of raising.
recommended_fix: Anchor the regex with $ (or a timezone/end component), or guard the cast so any remainder fails closed to false.

title: handle_take_over doc claims the write is 'ONLY taken_over_at' but the SQL also NULLs next_attempt_at and stamps updated_at
detail: The handler comment attributes sweep-exclusion solely to the SELECT filter while the SQL itself also NULLs next_attempt_at (the sql.gleam comment documents this as belt-and-braces). Two comments in the same feature disagree; the handler one is stale.
recommended_fix: Amend the handler doc to 'writes only taken_over_at + next_attempt_at = NULL + updated_at' to match the SQL.
